title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: US seeks to recover $1.1B in crypto stolen in North Korea-linked Binance hack
summary: US prosecutors are seeking control of stolen USDC, while Elliptic says hackers have moved $247 million through Bitcoin mixers.

title: Kalshi secures temporary win in New York gambling law dispute
summary: The ruling allows Kalshi to continue operating as its legal battle with New York over sports-related event contracts moves toward a January hearing.

title: BTCS offloads $44M in ETH to reduce DeFi debt amid market downturn
summary: BTCS sold more than half its Ether holdings to reduce leverage following the market sell-off, while BitMine added another 7,819 ETH to its treasury.

title: Base makes quantum security a 2027 priority as regulators warn of risks
summary: Base creator Jesse Pollak says the upcoming Everest upgrade will help prepare wallets for future quantum threats, although further changes will be needed.

title: Cuomo says rivals urged companies to opt out of OKXICE tokenized stocks
summary: Former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo said competitors encouraged companies to opt out of OKXICE’s rollout, while some issuers simply wanted more time.

title: Bitcoin rebounds 17% from $55K lows as Nvidia rally sparks $500M crypto liquidations
summary: Bitcoin price upside hit $64,500 as risk assets surged on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s reinstatement, while crypto liquidations topped $500 million four hours.

title: Cross River Bank enters Bitcoin-backed lending with $250K loans
summary: The US bank is offering Bitcoin-backed loans ranging from $10,000 to $250,000 through LendingUSA, allowing borrowers to access cash without selling their holdings.

title: How market depth shapes the price of a weekend Bitcoin sale
summary: Over 14 hours, Bitcoin traded on Kraken’s Canadian dollar market at an average 37.3% discount to a benchmark based on the exchange’s US dollar trades.

title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid ongoing intelligence probe
summary: Nvidia shares surged nearly 29% after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following consultations with the US government.
